sources: University of California Statewide IPM Program, Pest Notes: Black Widow and Other Widow Spiders: adult female has a red or orange hourglass on the underside of the large round abdomen; irregular, tough-stranded, sticky cobweb, hangs belly-up; found in dark, dry, sheltered, undisturbed places such as wood piles and garages; bite reactions range from mild to painful and serious, but death is very unlikely; males are smaller and their fangs are too small to break human skin; contrary to popular belief the female rarely eats the male after mating but may do so if hungry; https://ipm.ucanr.edu/PMG/PESTNOTES/pn7442.html

University of Wisconsin-Milwaukee Field Station, Bug of the Week, 'Speed-dating the Spiders: Black Widows': female venom is 15 times more toxic than that of a rattlesnake, but widows inject very little per bite; strong, messy, sticky, three-dimensional web; egg sacs contain about 250 eggs, up to nine sacs per summer; sibling cannibalism is rampant right after spiderlings emerge, only a small fraction survive; https://uwm.edu/field-station/bug-of-the-week/speed-dating-the-spiders-black-widows/

MedlinePlus (U.S. National Library of Medicine), Black widow spider bite: venom symptoms include muscle pain spreading from the bite to the whole body, very painful muscle cramps or spasms, increased sweating; https://medlineplus.gov/ency/article/002858.htm

NCBI Bookshelf / StatPearls, Black Widow Spider Toxicity: main toxin alpha-latrotoxin is a neurotoxin causing massive neurotransmitter release, producing pain, muscle rigidity, vomiting and sweating; https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK499987/

The Scientist, 'The Spider Lady, Circa 1939' (Nan Songer): human hair used for crosshairs in aircraft bombsights froze and broke at high altitude, so the US Bureau of Standards called for spider silk; her silk supplied bombsight crosshairs in World War II; Songer split black widow six-strand draglines into single strands with a needle to reach the width needed; https://www.the-scientist.com/the-spider-lady-circa-1939-70053
